name: Village at Homewood Point - Phase II
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: The Colorado Springs Housing Authority and MJT Properties are building Village at Homewood Point II, 83 one- and two-bedroom apartments for seniors 62+ at 40% to 60% AMI on housing authority land next to Phase I near downtown Colorado Springs; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $17.62M of CHFA bonds and broke ground in May 2025.
why_it_matters: It shows a housing authority keeping 100% ownership of a tax credit deal on its own land, with a private co-developer carrying guarantees, city HOME funds and fee rebates, and a county housing trust fund loan.

status.label: Under construction since about May 2025; leasing site says opening September 2026
status.detail: A local TV report dated 2025-06-27 quoted the housing authority saying the project broke ground the previous month. The property website (read 2026-10-21) says it is now open and taking applications, with opening planned for September 2026, and the city lists it with an opening of 2025. No certificate of occupancy or placed-in-service record was found.

next_step: Watch for a certificate of occupancy, placed-in-service date and lease-up reports from the Colorado Springs Housing Authority.

key_numbers.meaning: 50 one-bedroom and 33 two-bedroom units for ages 62+: 4 at 40%, 15 at 50% and 64 at 60% AMI.
About $15.8M over 10 years, plus $1,100,000 of state credit.
Tax-exempt bonds for a CHFA bond-financed loan, privately placed; CHFA also planned to be construction and permanent lender.

facts.value: 903 E. Colorado Ave, Colorado Springs 80903; directly west of Phase I, at East Pikes Peak Avenue and South Institute Street
Owned by the Colorado Springs Housing Authority; designated for multifamily use for about 18 years and previously approved by city planning
MX-M CR (mixed-use medium scale), 54 units per acre allowed; Development Plan and drainage report approved by city planning in February 2023

Four stories, two elevators, about 90,402 gross square feet (about 97,000 in a 2025 bid listing) with a podium garage; wood frame on post-tension foundation, hardboard siding and brick to match Phase I; solar shingles; EGC 2020 and electrification-ready
Qualified Census Tract; less than half a mile from Memorial Park, bus stop at Pikes Peak Avenue and Institute Street
100% owned by the Colorado Springs Housing Authority through the development; co-developer MJT Properties, Inc. provides all guarantees and compliance services
CHFA approved a cost basis override on 2023-06-28 (60% one-bedroom units hurt the cost basis calculation)

money.note: 2023 Round Two; the August 2023 applicant list showed $1,559,120 requested.

CHFA issuer and lender, private placement; the narrative also lists total bonds of $26.69M ($20M construction, $6.69M permanent) with no taxable bonds, figures that do not reconcile with the $17.62M tax-exempt amount.

money.source: City of Colorado Springs HOME funds
Other sources named in the application
money.note: El Paso County housing trust fund loan, solar tax credits, a CHFA permanent loan, Division of Housing soft funds (support letter) and a deferred developer fee; National Equity Fund gave a letter of interest as investor.

parties.name: Terra Management Group (per the leasing site; the application named the housing authority)

background.text: The project was submitted twice before; after CHFA feedback it was consolidated from two phases into one and 40% and 50% AMI units were added.
The Phase I environmental report found one historical condition, a jet fuel spill from a removed above-ground tank that was remediated and closed by the state oil and public safety division in 2008.
The market study rated marketability excellent and found no weaknesses; two other proposed senior tax credit projects were expected to lease up before this one opened.

A May 2021 site notice drew two neighbor inquiries (alley traffic, views, lighting, crime); the applicant said the alley will not be used and cited support letters from the city, county housing authority, Downtown Partnership and the mayor's office.
A February 2025 bid listing said all trades were awarded, construction was expected to start in March 2025 and take 15 months, Davis-Bacon wages apply and permitting was in process.

timeline.event: Notice of development posted at the site
Development Plan and drainage report approved by city planning
CHFA announces 2023 Round Two awards, including Village at Homewood Point - Phase II
Bid listing reports all trades awarded and a March 2025 start expected
Planned opening, per the leasing site

discrepancies.text: The city's Housing Solutions page lists the project as opened in 2025, while the property's own site gives a September 2026 opening and the groundbreaking was reported in May 2025.
The application said the housing authority would manage the property, while the leasing site names Terra Management Group.
The application gives the building as 90,402 gross square feet, while a 2025 bid listing describes about 97,000 square feet.

open_questions: Bond closing date, final equity investor and price, and total development cost.
Amount of the El Paso County housing trust fund loan and whether Division of Housing funds were awarded (not confirmed by a reachable public page).
Ground lease or land contribution terms from the housing authority and the property tax treatment.
Certificate of occupancy and placed-in-service dates.
No public site plan in a planning packet was found; the leasing site's images are labeled AI-generated renderings and were not used.
